sources.entry: Razzia - Quiz game platform, designed for smaller self-hosted events (alternative to Kahoot!). MIT Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: Razzia is an open-source quiz platform that you host on your own server for smaller events, as a self-hosted alternative to Kahoot!.
summary.what_it_does: Razzia lets a manager host live quiz games on their own server. The manager logs into a management interface with a password set via MANAGER_PASSWORD, then shares a game URL and room code so participants can join. Quizzes and results are stored as files in a ./config folder, which is created on first run with an example quiz and can be edited from the host. The README describes a documentation set covering configuration, quiz structure, custom branding, reverse proxy setup, a WebSocket protocol for custom clients (such as an ESP32 physical buzzer), and an HTTP API for sessions, quiz and result management, and game creation. It can be run with Docker or directly with Node.js and pnpm.
use_cases: host a quiz game for a small event
run live quizzes for a classroom or meetup
build a physical buzzer client for a quiz
store and edit quizzes as local files
how_to_run: Create a compose.yml with the razzia image, port 3000:3000, a ./config volume, and env_file .env
Without Docker: requires Node.js 24 and pnpm 10.16+; run pnpm install
Copy .env.example to .env and set MANAGER_PASSWORD (WEB_PORT default 3000, SOCKET_PORT default 3001)
Run pnpm build then pnpm start
notable: Designed for smaller self-hosted events rather than large-scale use
Quizzes and results persist as editable files in a mounted config folder
Documented WebSocket protocol allows building custom clients such as an ESP32 buzzer
Documented HTTP API for sessions, quizzes, results, and game creation
Available as a Docker image on Docker Hub and GHCR
caveats: Intended for smaller events, according to the README
Non-Docker setup requires Node.js 24 and pnpm 10.16+
